author: Plato
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Plato saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?

originalQuote: Democracy is next to oligarchy in the order of the forms of government, and it is the most beautiful of the imperfect forms of government, but it is not the best. For it is not possible for the many, or for the poor, to govern the city in excellence, but they can do so in a manner that is not bad. And when democracy has been established, it is next to be transformed into tyranny, for the demos is not able to govern itself, but it is ruled by the worst of men.
